summary: This page formalizes generative learning tasks for graphs, distinguishing between graph encoders (graph to embeddings) and decoders (embeddings to graphs). It outlines the utility of graph generation for understanding formation processes and predicting new structures, such as molecules or brain connectivity graphs. The content details the machine learning basics for self-supervised generation, focusing on density estimation via maximum likelihood and sampling from noise distributions. Finally, it presents a comprehensive taxonomy of deep graph generation methods, categorizing them into unconditional and conditional approaches with specific sequential and one-shot techniques.

parsed.summary: This page formalizes generative learning tasks for graphs, distinguishing between graph encoders (graph to embeddings) and decoders (embeddings to graphs). It outlines the utility of graph generation for understanding formation processes and predicting new structures, such as molecules or brain connectivity graphs. The content details the machine learning basics for self-supervised generation, focusing on density estimation via maximum likelihood and sampling from noise distributions. Finally, it presents a comprehensive taxonomy of deep graph generation methods, categorizing them into unconditional and conditional approaches with specific sequential and one-shot techniques.
